# Feast of Blood

*Pages PDF 3-28*

## **Welcome to Spider Holt**
In the east of Stirland lies the cursed land of Sylvania, a region of mountainous crags and dark forests. Many of its evil woods are widely known: Hunger Wood, Tangle Wood, Ghoul Wood, names hinting at horrors lurking within. There are more obscure woods, not found on maps but familiar to locals. The Bloated Copse and Toadstool Thicket are but two of several obscure woods, known by Sylvanian folk to never venture into unless your life depended on it. Spider Holt is another. 

## **Lorenz of Red Moss Tower**
Spiders are not alone in the wood. One vampire is brave enough to live within it, albeit at the edge on the other side from Hagedorn. Lorenz of Red Moss Tower is a Necrarch, one of uglier forms of vampire-kind. His existence in their land is tolerated by the von Carsteins as his talents have proven useful to them. Furthermore, once a decade Lorenz throws a damn good party! All manner of night-stalkers are invited. 

Spider Holt lies on the Sylvanian side of the OstermarkStirland border. The inhabitants of the hamlet of Hagedorn on the Ostermark side know that Sylvania’s forests conceal more than one variety of fanged, blood-sucking predator. No one knows how many long-legged terrors lurk within Spider Holt, but everyone knows that after pushing a few hundred yards through the tangled branches you see the first of the threads and webs, almost luminous, spreading from branch to branch, covering the ground, becoming ever thicker. Only the brave stray across the border to collect wood, and even they only skirt the edges. 

Folk say Spider Holt is feared even by vampires, whose bloodfilled corpses are a temptation for any spider. That a rumoured Spider Baron lives in the heart of the wood, a monster who was once a man or vampire, whose arms and legs were sliced in twain lengthways by the Blood God as a blessing or a curse. That there is a deep pit, white with webs, from which all the spiders of the world crawl. That if you bring the spiders a suitable offering, they may let you go with your life and a gift only spiders can give. 

It is time for this decade’s ball, and Lorenz has his servants busily preparing. However, Lorenz wants something grotesque as his special course, a challenge even to his guests’ jaded appetites. He wonders, who among the invited shall be first to dare to taste the blood of a live Giant Spider? 

Lorenz prefers not to risk his living servants in obtaining a spider. Instead, he has sent his Scarecrows, but they are blunt instruments and have been unsuccessful. When Lorenz becomes aware of the Characters roaming Spider Holt, he decides to blackmail them into doing the job. If the adventurers succeed in securing him a plump, live Giant Spider, Lorenz ensures they stay for the party. 

## **The Spider Baron**
The Spider Baron is real. A disturbing Human-Spider Mutant, he leads a community of Giant Spiders and Human-Spider Mutants deep within the woods. Like most spiders, he and his followers prefer to remain out of sight. They have more reason to be scared of people than people have to be scared of them. 

On discovering Lorenz’s scheme, the Spider Baron has other ideas. He has long been aware of Lorenz, but is unaware he is a Vampire, believing him only to be a powerful Wizard. By placing one of their own kind in the heart of Lorenz’s home may let the spiders play a game of their own. Perhaps the Characters can help the spiders when they know the plan; perhaps the spiders won’t tell them the plan, and they’ll face yet another horror in the woods. 

## **Getting the Characters Involved**
As the GM, you must get the Characters into a situation where Lorenz can persuade or force them to brave the depths of Spider Holt and capture a live Giant Spider. You may have ideas of your own, but here it is assumed the Characters have reason to travel to, or at least through, the village of Hagedorn on the Ostermark side of the Ostermark-Stirland border. However, the setting can be relocated if necessary. 

## **Hagedorn, Tobias and the White Hart**
Hagedorn’s Priest, Tobias, has had a dream he interpreted as a vision from Taal. He saw a White Hart trapped in the folds of a great web; a thousand black eyes glinted in the surrounding dark. Something is trapped, something important to Taal. Whatever it is, it must be saved. Tobias is too old to brave the terrors of the wood, but perhaps others could accompany Esther, his initiate and successor. 

Tobias sees the arrival of the Characters as a literal godsend, and his friendly welcome is a prelude to telling them of his vision and asking them to rescue the White Hart. Tobias first attempts to persuade them with the notion of a spiritually noble quest. If the Characters remain reluctant, he tries spiritual bribery **(** _‘Taal would be most pleased and generous to those who aid those dear to Him’_ ). If this fails, he resorts to spiritual blackmail. Dire warnings of Taal’s anger may be ignored, but after leaving Hagedorn, unhelpful Characters encounter the most atrocious rain and wind, seemingly following them wherever they go, uprooted trees falling across their path – the conditions lessen and relent when they decide to head back to Hagedorn. If the Characters refuse to be coerced, let them go, but if they ever need aid from Taal or his followers, they encounter distrust and unhelpfulness until they perform a penance of some sort. 

If the Characters accept the task, however reluctantly, Tobias claps them on the back and tells them legends of Spider Wood (see **Welcome to Spider Wood** ). Tobias seems oblivious to the fears these tales might raise, believing the Characters’ agreement spiritually binds them to the task, and backing out rouses Taal’s anger.

## **Esther**
be assumed dead, eaten by spiders, but remembered fondly by Tobias and the villagers for her bravery and devotion to Taal. 

Tobias introduces the Characters to his initiate, Esther, a pleasant, ordinary young woman with dark eyes, fair hair and complexion. She is friendly, interested in the Characters, but a little quiet, following Tobias’s lead. She is strong and fit, unsurprising in a vocational follower of the god of the wilds. 

Of course, the true meaning of Tobias’s dream remains to be seen. 

This introduction brings the Characters to both Lorenz’s and the Giant Spiders’ attention. Lorenz’s agents in the wood (the creepy **Scarecrows** ) inform him of the Characters’ exploration of the wood and he uses them to kidnap Esther. Lorenz uses the promise of her freedom, and maybe a modest reward, to persuade the Characters to help him. Meanwhile, the spiders recognise Esther for what she is, and the Spider Baron has had a vision of his own… 

She is keen to venture into the woods, but for her own reasons. Unknown to anyone, Esther has been changing. Some nights she senses the tremors of every secret footstep and restless sleeper in the hamlet. Spiky white hairs are growing on her legs and arms, pale enough that no one has noticed _yet_ . Once, her mouth stretched wide and pincer-like fangs grew out before receding. Esther is not worried: she believes Taal is blessing her, bringing her closer to nature. She is not stupid: she knows the word Mutant, that she is slowly changing forever, and cannot stay in Hagedorn.

## **Time in Hagedorn**
The Characters can head into Spider Holt straightaway, but may wait a while to prepare, and talk to the locals. Hagedorn is a small village: a handful of thatched cottages, a small shrinecum-temple topped with huge antlers where Tobias and Esther live (with curtained-off quarters), two communal sheds for animals and crops, and a blacksmith’s forge. The buildings are surrounded by an angled wall of outward-facing sharpened stakes – an untested defence against the spiders of the wood. Beyond this are communal fields, worked by the villagers. Folk are friendly and curious, but easily intimidated. 

Besides Tobias and Esther, the Characters should meet Hugo, Hagedorn’s blacksmith and carpenter. Hugo would be the hamlet’s leader if not for his deep respect for Tobias. Hugo is strong and brave, but won’t follow the Characters and Esther into Spider Holt; everyone recognises Hugo’s duty is to Hagedorn and its people. However, Hugo gladly assists Characters if they try building spider traps later in the adventure. 

## **Into the Woods**
Spider Holt is dark and shadowy, full of tangled branches and sticky cobwebs that soon adorn the Characters’ clothes and tickle their faces. Despite what they’ve been told, the cobwebs don’t become thicker the deeper they travel, but they are everywhere. There is enough light to see by day, but a torch or lantern is sometimes needed. During their explorations, the Characters find small clearings open to the sun where it feels safe to stop and rest. Spider Holt is not completely devoid of animal life, but there is less birdsong inside the wood than in the fields outside. Small, harmless spiders are everywhere; Characters suffering from arachnophobia ( **WFRP** , page 191) may have a difficult time. 

Let the Characters spend some time searching Spider Holt for a White Hart, even though there’s no such creatures to find. Instead, there are several encounters to keep the Characters occupied. If the Characters return to Hagedorn each night, that’s fine. A few days in the woods provides a credible amount of time for Lorenz to notice the Characters and make plans to use them, and for the spiders to notice Esther. 

During this time, Esther is periodically distracted, but cheerful. She happily handles the small spiders scuttling around with no fear at all. Although she intends to mysteriously vanish, she won’t do so immediately. Of course, she is kidnapped by Lorenz’s servants soon enough, but whether this happens just after she sneaks off or during a more dramatic confrontation between the Characters and Lorenz’s servants depends on circumstances (see **Lorenz Makes His Move** ). 

## Fire
Sooner or later, Characters will use fire to clear cobwebs or intimidate and attack spiders. It is inevitable. However, emphasise dryness in Spider Holt. Cobwebs burn easily, but in places where they are very thick (where the Characters are most likely to use fire), old branches and moss go up in flames too. (Smoke from burning branches and moss will make the Characters’ eyes water, so allow more time for them to navigate the wood with blurred vision.) You don’t have to stop the Characters using fire or burn down the forest, just make them feel it’s a risk. Also, fire causes the viscous fluids in a spider’s abdomen to boil and explode with a significant pop. It won’t work with big ones, but if the Characters are faced with hundreds of little spiders and apply a flaming torch, the resulting pops as their carapaces explode are startling. The smell is nauseating and the scent of burning will linger for a long time. Remember to cover the Characters’ faces with harmless but sticky spider shrapnel. 

## **Itsy Bitsy Spiders**
There are lots of small spiders crawling about, so make use of them. Minor events: 

- spiders drop from branches and crawl over the Characters, creeping through gaps in their armour; **Challenging Cool (+0%)** Test to resist stripping armour and clothes 

- sleeping Characters wake to find a fist-sized spider with a lot of eyes sitting on their chest looking at them; it’s big but runs instead of biting 

- random Character is bitten by some nasty-looking little green spiders; very itchy but not venomous (–1SL to Tests requiring concentration for 1d10 hours, but _not_ during combat) 

- a bird is trapped in a dense web. If the Characters help it, scores of harmless spiders boil out of a hole in the tree, and begin wrapping the bird. Further attempts to rescue the bird results in the spiders scuttling about in a scary fashion; a successful **Hard (–20%) Cool** Test is needed to save the bird. 

- Characters acting aggressively towards smaller spiders have a 50% chance of being bitten, with a 50% chance of bites being venomous. Treat venom effects as random Conditions: _Bleeding_ ; _Blinded_ 5; _Broken_ ; _Fatigued_ ; _Poisoned_ (Easy or Average Venom); _Prone_ ( **Average (+20%) Toughness** Test every minute to recover and stand up); _Stunned_ ; _Unconscious_ ( **Average (+20%) Toughness** Test every minute to remove condition). 

Some possible events and encounters in Spider Holt to keep the Characters interested are described below. These can occur before or after the Characters undertake the mission for Lorenz. 

## **Tangled**
Run this before **Lorenz Makes His Move** . Characters find what appears to be several corpses tangled in webs. Closer inspection reveals they are scarecrows with pumpkin heads. Only if a deeper examination is made (clothes removed, stuffing pulled, inevitable small spiders) do the Characters discover a driedout heart nailed to the crosspiece of the body, and that limbs and fingers are properly jointed and tied together with sinew. Both Players and Character likely recognise these are magical constructs, although if they imagine they’re the work of a murderous folk artist let them think that. A successful **Average (+20) Lore (Magick)** Test or **Challenging (+0) Intelligence** Test suggests that dislodging the nailed heart would disrupt the magic animating them (see **Lorenz’s Scarecrow Men** for more). If you wish, one entrapped Scarecrow is partially active and attempts to grapple any Character inspecting it. It seeks to _Entangle_ only. 

## **A Forest Pool**
The Characters find a clearing. In the centre is a pool of water with a thorny, berrying bush beside it. On the ground, covering the entire clearing, is an opaque layer of white, non-sticky cobweb; hidden underneath are several empty holes about 2-ft deep and 1–2-ft wide. This place is a trap for larger animals, and Players can probably tell it’s a set-up. However, it demonstrates the spiders’ intelligence. If the Characters risk going to the tree and pool, they can avoid the pit holes by poking the web as they go; if they don’t take simple precautions feel free to let someone fall in; a failed **Challenging (+0) Agility** Test is good for a single Wound and a sore ankle. There are a few Giant Spiders secretly watching. This is an opportunity for a combat encounter; there are as many spiders as Characters ( **WFRP** , page 315, Size (Small) Trait), but they retreat after one of their number are killed. 

## **Temptation**
This looks like a trap, but it’s not. Within a tangle of dead branches and dusty cobwebs, the Characters see an old leather satchel stuck on a branch. A crumpled and vaguely corpse-like form covered with old web lies beneath. Characters with Skills like Outdoor Survival, Track, or Set Trap should be allowed a **Difficult (–10)** Test to recognise this as a long-unused spider nest. If none of them realise this, Esther can point it out. Hopefully the Characters are tempted to go for the satchel, the contents of which are left in your hands. However, no matter how carefully they try to take the satchel, its removal dislodges the old shed skin of a Halfling-sized Giant Spider, which falls from above right on top of them. Try to scare them by treating it like a combat; let them make a few attacks. Then, once they realise, scare them again by pointing out just how bloody big these things are. 

## **Lorenz Makes His Move**
Esther’s kidnapping takes place when she is separated from the Characters: trailing behind examining a plant, when taking a turn at watch, or answering a call of nature. Remember Esther is planning to run away, so is seeking such opportunities herself. If the Characters become engrossed in a problem or argument, a silent kidnapping could take place: allow the Characters an **Average (+20) Perception** Test to notice she is missing, or just wait until someone mentions her by name. After some panic and frantic searching, Lorenz’s Scarecrows appear, and Lorenz speaks through them as described below. 

_‘Stay your hands, my friends! The lady will_ not _be harmed. I have taken her as mere leverage. You see, I need your assistance._ 

_‘I throw a memorable party every now and again, at my home in the forest, and my guests expect something mysterious to stir their interest. This year, I’ve decided on a Geheimnisnacht theme, and I want a live Giant Spider as my surprise of the evening! Just think of the sensation it will cause._ 

_‘My Scarecrows are obedient, but cannot improvise and have been outwitted by these cunning spiders. I need your skill and wit to obtain the prize! So, the deal is this: catch me a Giant Spider! Alive; that’s essential. With a body that would fill a wheelbarrow. Bring it to this spot within one week and my minions will lead you to my home._ 

_‘And you never know, besides the return of the lady, there may be a reward or two!’_ 

The Characters may have questions: 

## **Who Are You?**
_‘I am Lorenz of Red Moss Tower.’_ 

## **What Are You?**
_‘I am a wizard of some modest skill. I would have hoped that much is clear.’_ 

## **Are You a Vampire?**
For a more dramatic kidnapping, Lorenz uses two teams of Scarecrows. A smaller group of three grabs Esther and vanishes through the trees; while a team of eight gets between them and the Characters, preventing them from following. If necessary, they attempt to draw as many Characters away from Esther as possible, giving them noises or glimpses to investigate. 

The eight Scarecrows don’t attack the Characters, but attempt to stall them. If attacked, they fight defensively. Lorenz speaks magically through the Scarecrows, probably giving the Characters cause to hesitate. 

_‘Ha! I dabble in necromancy and I live in Sylvania, but I am no von Carstein bloodsucker. I live here on their sufferance, as I am sometimes of use to them.’_ 

## **You Dabble in Necromancy?**
_‘Yes, though I prefer the Jade Winds. Sticks and dried flowers are dead things, too, and can be animated like bones and dead flesh.’_ 

## **Where Have You Taken Esther? What Are You Doing with Her?**
_‘To my home, Red Moss Tower. She will be safe and unharmed, an honoured guest, even if you fail.’_ 

## **Have You Seen a White Hart in the Woods?**
_‘A white heart? Oh, you mean a deer. No, I have not. Is that what you seek? Interesting.’_ 

## **How Do We Catch a Giant Spider?**
_‘A large jar and a sheet of parchment?_ Great Sigmar! _I’m blackmailing you to avoid having to think about this myself. Now hop to it!’_ 

## **The Scarecrows**
Scarecrows are Lorenz’s foot soldiers. They are built from yew branches, jointed and bound together with gut and sinew, topped off with a roughly-carved pumpkin head. A dried-out human heart is nailed to the central cross with a rusty coffin nail. They are dressed in peasant rags and sacking, stuffed with straw and dried leaves. Some have candles inside their heads, adding to their creepiness on a dark night. They are modestly intelligent for artificial undead creatures, and follow fairly complex orders well, but have little initiative. What is carved into their orange faces provides an illusion of emotion. 

Some wield swords, some bows; all are capable of operating simple devices, like bolts, locks and keys. 

They have a weakness: if the nailed heart is dislodged, the magic animating them is disrupted. Dislodging the heart requires a Critical Wound to the chest. This can happen through the luck of the dice, but a successful called shot ( **Hard (–20) Weapon Skill** Test) to the chest avoids a roll on the Hit Locations table. 

If he concentrates, Lorenz can see through a Scarecrow’s eyes, but only one Scarecrow at a time. He can also speak through up to half a dozen of them from several miles away if they are reasonably close together (within a large room, a forest clearing). 

## **The Great Spider Hunt**
So how _do_ you catch a Giant Spider alive? That’s up to the Characters and they have a week. Whatever plans they come up with (cage traps, knock-out gas, magic, pit-traps, big nets, chasing with flaming torches, hunting dogs, the power of prayer) let them implement them. If the plans are good, give them a fair chance to succeed. If they’re terrible, give them a fair chance to surprise everyone. There’s potentially a lot of fun here, but let the Players take the lead. Hagedorn’s inhabitants enthusiastically offer suggestions and help in construction of traps and cages. However, some **Hard (–20) Charm** or **Leadership** Tests are required before any are willingly venture too deeply into Spider Holt, perhaps to position a trap. A similar **Very Hard (–30)** Test is needed to persuade any to stay and help. **Intimidation** results in fear and resentment. 

At some point, the Characters experience either success (spectacular or lucky) or a dramatic failure (embarrassing or frustrating). Or, it might only be a day or two to go until Lorenz’s deadline and the Characters have nothing to show for it. Now the other power in Spider Holt makes himself known: the Spider Baron.

## **The Spider Baron’s Emissary**
By now, the Characters are probably used to the presence of handsized and smaller spiders everywhere, so they may not notice a gradual increase in the number of glittering black eyes all around or the intensified sound of scuttling, creeping and crawling. They might be returning to Hagedorn after another failure or heading to Lorenz’s meeting point with their prize, but allow them a **Difficult (–10) Perception** Test to notice ( **Challenging (–0)** if anyone specifically mentions being extra wary). 

If Characters spot the build-up and are on their guard, the Spider Baron’s Emissary approaches them alone, carrying a white cloth of peace (although they are discreetly surrounded). If they don’t spot the build-up, they are suddenly and obviously surrounded by a great many spiders, some just the size Lorenz was after. This likely gives all but a Troll Slayer pause for thought. The Emissary again carries the white cloth, but if the Characters fight, so be it. The spiders fight defensively and seek to _Entangle_ the Characters with webs. Give the Characters a fair fight, but unless the Characters are cunning, brutal or lucky, sheer numbers win the day. After this, they can be carried directly to a meeting with the Spider Baron himself. 

If the Characters restrain themselves or surrender, the Emissary steps forward: a tall, lean man wearing black armour ( **Average (+20) Perception** Test to notice it’s made of spider carapace and silk), carrying a spear. He has very dark, very round eyes, but seems Human. He raises a hand so as to halt or silence the Characters. He speaks: 

_‘You are servants of the White Queen?’_ 

This should lead to some questions and answers. 

## **Who Is the White Queen?**
_‘The woman you escorted in the woods. Our eyes in the trees say you failed to protect her from the Branchmen. Why do you hunt us?_ We _did not take her.’_ 

## **Why Do You Want Esther? the White Queen?**
_‘She is to be our Queen. The Baron has foreseen it in a vision. We seek only to bring her safely to him.’_ 

## **We Have a Problem. Can You Help?**

## **At the Court of the Spider Baron**
Travelling willingly or trussed up in silk and carried by spiders, the Characters are taken to meet the Spider Baron. If any Character asks to ride a Giant Spider, several narrow-waisted spiders have no objection. For those with the Ride Skill, it’s a wild ride; those without it must make a **Challenging (+0) Agility** Test to stay on. If they fall, they are uninjured, but the Emissary suggests being tied back on with silk. If Characters decline, the spiders move more slowly. The slow pace creates a disjointed rocking movement, which makes the rider feel like they are at sea. The movement combined with the spiders’ horrendous cloak of earthy, sticky-sweet odor is bound to make the rider feel queasy. 

The Characters are taken deeper into the wood than they’ve before. They see more evidence of larger spiders and their lairs: ominous web-tunnels, nests of sticks and webs, wrapped prey with protruding tails, claws or wings, and large woolly bundles ( **Easy (+10) Intelligence** Test to identify as egg-sacs). They are observed by spiders of many sizes, one as large as a cart. The Emissary advises them, _‘Don’t be frightened. Most of them are more scared of you than you are of them.’_ 

Eventually, the forest opens into a large, rocky clearing, one end rising steeply into a cliff-like outcropping reaching above the trees. In the cliff face are many dark holes at different heights. They appear carved and some of the lower ones even have ladders leading down from them. At ground level, the cliff face is dominated by one huge web tunnel, thick with grey webs, leading into darkness. If the Characters were captured for their journey here, they are now unbound. 

Answer any questions the Players have regarding their surroundings, but if they start asking more questions about the Baron or what’s going to happen, the Emissary responds simply: 

## _‘Be Patient. Be Still.’_
Slowly, the inhabitants emerge from the smaller caves. Most are Giant Spiders, though a handful are Humans. However, many of the Spiders and all of the Humans are Mutants. Among the Spiders, Characters see oddly human eyes, not glassy black ones. One has a set of palps ending in human hands. Another grows long plaits of auburn hair. Ears on legs. Oversized human teeth instead of fangs. Among the Human Mutants, Characters see extra limbs, spiky-haired torsos, bulging black eyes, clicking mouthparts, or patterned skin. As they climb from their caves, they gather silently either side of the largest cave entrance and observe the Characters. Other spiders appear from the woods around them. The earthy, sickly-sweet smell intensifies making the air feel oppressive.

## _‘Be Patient. Be Still.’_
There is deathly silence and stillness. If the Characters are not already intently watching the large cave, their attention is drawn to it. Something is moving in the darkness. They see a hint of legs. Long, hairy legs probing the webs of the dark tunnel. A sparkle as black eyes catch the light. A monstrous Giant Spider crouches in its den. It pauses. Have each Character make a **Difficult (–10%) Perception** Test: successful observers realise there is more here than is immediately obvious; give them time to share this information with their less observant fellows. 

## **Human-Spider Mutants**

**Traits:** Variable due to Mutation, but at least two of: Arboreal, Armour 1 or 2, Bite +6, Fast, Fear 1, Night Vision, Venom (Average), Weapon +7, Web 40 

And then it appears. And stands upright, perhaps 7-ft tall. 

The Spider Baron is a Mutant, though whether mutated man or mutated spider is uncertain. From belly down he is human, even wearing trousers and boots (a little outdated and ill fitting, but an impressive eye-catching colour all the same). Upwards, his belly and chest transform into a body at once both human and spider. There are two long limbs on either side. On the left both are fully spider, on the right the upper is spider-like and the lower is human, though covered with spiky hair, and carrying a long sword. The upper chest and shoulders carry a monstrous spider’s head, with five large black eyes around the crown and a pair of horrendously large mandibles. 

After a moment’s stillness, this monstrosity strides quickly towards the Characters and the Emissary, but stops halfway between them and his cave. At any time from his emergence up to this point, it’s reasonable to inflict the Spider Baron’s _Terror_ Trait and have Characters make **Cool** Tests. Any Character who gains one or more _Broken_ Conditions and flees can be contained by the surrounding spiders until other Characters come to their aid. This may lead to conflict, but hopefully things quickly calm. 

The Spider Baron and his Mutant followers combine the traits of Humans and Giant Spider. 

## **A Civilised Conversation**
Though the Mutants with Human mouths can speak (like the Emissary), they and the Spiders communicate through gesture and vibration. Regardless of what happens after the Spider Baron’s emergence, a conversation between him and the Characters takes place in the clearing. However, as the Baron has no human mouth, the Emissary translates for the Characters. Somehow, the Baron understands the Characters. The Baron gestures with his limbs, clicks his mandibles and taps or stamps his feet (sometimes with a jaunty rhythm). He has a simple question: 

_‘Where is she? Where is my Queen?’_ 

The course of this conversation depends on how open the Characters are with the Baron. The Baron himself is open and honest, but his focus is solely on gaining his Queen. He is not interested in answering questions about himself or his people until a rescue plan is in place. 

If the Characters haven’t already explained, he wants to know what they and his Queen were doing in his woods in the first place. If they tell him about Tobias’s vision of the White Hart trapped in webs, the Baron shares his own vision: that of a giant white-furred spider caught in a wooden cage. Should a Character ask what the cage looked like, the Baron draws with his sword in the dirt something reminiscent of one of the buildings in Hagedorn, crucially topped-off with what looks like a pair of antlers. If they don’t recall it themselves, allow the Characters a **Challenging (+0) Intelligence** Test to remember the antlers on Hagedorn’s shrine-cum-temple to Taal. 

If the Characters fail to make the connection, allow them a **Challenging (+0) Intelligence** Test: the two visions suggest that Esther is both the White Hart and the White Queen. 

## **Plans Within Plans**
The Spiders know of Lorenz, but are unaware of his vampiric nature, believing him a powerful wizard. He lives in a red-walled tower on the opposite edge of the wood from Hagedorn, within a strange garden that blooms all year round with a variety of magnificent red fragrant flowers. There are several buildings, and he seems to have Human servants as well as many Scarecrows. 

The Spider Baron and (hopefully) the Characters agree that Esther must be saved. A full-scale assault might be suggested; after all, there are _a lot_ of spiders. However, they won’t do anything to risk the Queen’s life. The Baron is adamant on this point. 

Giving Lorenz what he wants may be the safest approach, and the Spiders are in the position to give it to him. Hopefully, this would get the Characters inside the tower, close to Esther and conclude in a daring escape. 

Aim to let the players realise this for themselves, before the Baron suggests it. 

The Baron has a cunning twist to this plan. Whether or not he shares this with the Characters depends greatly on their behaviour towards him and his subjects. He understands that Humans fear and kill spiders. That’s part of the natural order and he won’t hold it against them too much. So, there’s a 95% chance that he’ll share the plan with them. This is reduced if they: 

- fought and had to be captured by the Emissary and his Spiders (–10%) 

- have been rude to him – barons deserve respect (–5 to –10% depending on the insult, for each rude Character) 

- insulted Esther (–20%) 

- attacked the Spiders/Emissary/Baron within their own territory (–30/40/50% respectively) 

The Baron’s plan is simple. The Giant Spider he provides is a Trojan Horse. The gravid female is filled to bursting with thousands of small mutant spiders with unusually large fangs and appetites to match. 

Whether the Spider Baron shares this detail with the Characters or not, the rest of the plan is simple enough. The Characters can carry the trussed-up spider to meet with Lorenz’s Scarecrows. The Emissary and other Spiders follow discreetly and hide around the border of Lorenz’s territory for a week. 

## **In Lorenz’s Garden**
With a trussed spider, the Characters head to the appointed place to meet Lorenz’s Scarecrows. A Scarecrow silently beckons them to follow and leads a twisty route to Lorenz’s home. As they get closer, they observe two things: the cobwebs thin-out and there is an increasing number of Yew trees. A **Very** – **Hard ( 30) Perception** Test is needed to see any hint of the Emissary and Spiders accompanying them. 

Lorenz’s home lies within an extremely large clearing. However, this clearing is a beautiful garden, with well maintained green lawns, clean stone paths and yew hedging, rose gardens, flower beds and even vegetable plots. A stream flows in one side and out the other, with a picturesque wooden bridge arching over it. The smell of rich scented roses and fresh herbs is delectable and almost soporific — a sharp contrast to the odor in the depths of Spider Holt. Scarecrows patrol the boundaries, although there are seemingly ordinary people tending the vegetables and flower-beds. They look up briefly from their beans and carrots when the Characters pass, wave, then get back to work. 

Even in winter, the garden is colourful: there are winterflowering plants, yellow conifers and berrying shrubs. After days of grey lichen and web-shrouded gloom, this is a magical place. Literally in fact: Characters with Second Sight automatically see the garden is vibrant with _Ghyran_ , the Jade Wind. This gives a +20 modifier to Casting and Channelling Tests related to the Lore of Life. However, allow players with Second Sight a **Hard (–20) Perception** Test. Success reveals a subtle undercurrent of _Dhar_ , Dark Magic. 

Spending time in the garden reveals this subtle undercurrent more physically: 

- bushes rustle without evidence of animals or birds, grasses sway without breeze 

- out of the corner of the eye, flowers turn to look at passing Characters 

- walking down a clear path, a Character trips over a root or branch that suddenly juts out 

- a tendril grasps a Character, seemingly grabbing a wrist/ belt/scabbard 

- a Character is scratched by a rose or thorny bush, even though they weren’t that close. 

These events are unsettling, but harmless. If Lorenz is asked, he observes, _‘Yes, some of the plants are a bit suspicious of strangers. I’ll have a word.’_ 

Towards one edge of the garden is a yellow-coloured stone tower patchy with a red-tinged moss. Windows suggest four levels, topped-off with a red-tiled conical roof. Annexing the tower is a moss-free rectangular building of the same stone with a similarly tiled roof. With arched windows, it looks like some kind of hall. Both structures are ornamented with hanging baskets and window boxes. It is surrounded by a wide, gravelled area. If Players with Second Sight direct it upon the tower, a successful **Hard (–20) Perception** Test suggests the presence of _Dhar_ underneath both the tower and the hall. 

On the other side of the clearing from where the Characters enter, initially hidden by the tower, is an opening in the edge of the clearing. From it, a road wide enough for a carriage, leads out of the woods into Sylvania. This is the route most of Lorenz’s party guests use on arriving for the party. 

## **Meeting Lorenz**
Their Scarecrow escort leads the Characters with their spider through the garden towards the tower. Before they reach it, double doors fly open in the attached hall and a tall figure in flowing dark-green robes emerges and heads quickly towards them, arms raised wide in friendly greeting. As he nears them, anyone with Magical Sense can, if they ask, make an **Average (+20) Intuition** Test. Success shows him to be a powerful wizard. An Astounding success (+6) reveals his Channelling Specialisation is both _Dhar_ and _Ghyran_ . If anyone asks to use their Second Sight while looking at him, allow a **Difficult (–10) Perception** Test. Success reveals a breeze of _Ghyran_ swirling around him (they are seeing the magic of the perfumes (mainly a classic rose scent, in case you are wondering) he uses to disguise his true Necarch features. Something else they might notice ( **Challenging (+0) Perception** Test) is that Lorenz’s sleeves only come down to his elbows and there is soil on his forearms and dirt under his nails: this man is an avid gardener. 

_‘Welcome to my home and garden! You’ve been successful, I see! Wonderful! You’ll be wanting to see Esther, of course. Here, let my servants take the spider and I’ll take you up to her.’_ 

At this point Lorenz claps his hands and three people and a couple of Scarecrows come from the hall and relieve the Characters of the spider, taking it to the hall. The people smile and acknowledge the Characters in a normal, friendly way, but say nothing beyond a quick _‘hello’_ or _‘she’s a beauty!’_ 

_‘Don’t worry, they’ll keep it safe. Incredible beastie! You’ll have to tell me how you caught it.’_ 

Lorenz chats on and on as he leads them to the tower doorway. 

_‘Do avoid touching the moss. It has a habit of eating people.’_ 

Scattered around the garden are smaller, single-level buildings that if explored turn out to be: a wood shed for gardening equipment, a stone building with a cool cellar for storing fruit and vegetables, a dormitory with a kitchen for a dozen or more Human servants and a workshop for carpentry, blacksmithing and masonry. 

## **Lorenz — Necrarch Vampire**

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | 60 | 43 | 46 | 40 | 66 | 64 | 40 | 73 | 62 | 40 | 23 |

**Traits:** Dark Vision, Distracting (when not using Potion of Beauty), Fear (when not using Potion of Beauty), Painless, Regeneration 

**Skills:** Animal Care 70, Channelling (Ghyran, Dhar) 72, Charm 55, Cool 67, Dodge 68, Evaluate 74, Gossip 45, Heal 74, Intimidate 50, Intuition 68, Language (Battle) 77, Language (Bretonnian) 75, Language (Magick) 82, Language (Wastelander) 74, Leadership 50, Lore (Herbs) 80, Lore (Magic) 80, Lore (Plants) 80, Lore (Reikland) 75, Lore (Warfare) 75, Melee (Basic) 63, Melee (Polearm) 61, Perception 70, Ride (Horse) 65, Trade (Herbalist) 49, Trade (Poisons) 41 

**Talents:** Aethyric Attunement 4, Arcane Magic (Dark, Life), Concoct 5, Craftsman (Herbalist) 3, Detect Artefact, Dual Wielder 3, Fast Hands 3, Flee! 5, Hardy 2, Instinctive Diction, Magical Sense 5, Master Tradesman (Herbalist) 3, Menacing 2, Petty Magic, Read/Write, Savant (Plants) 6, Second Sight 4, Sixth Sense 4 

**Spells:** Petty: Bearings, Careful Step, Drain, Gust, Light, Open Lock, Purify Water, Rot, Sleep, Spring 

**Arcane:** Aethyric Armour, Breath, Bridge, Distracting, Drop, Entangle, Ward 

**Life:** Barkskin, Earthblood, Earthpool, Fat of the Land, Forest of Thorns, Lie of the Land, Lifebloom, Regenerate **Necromancy:** Raise Dead, Reanimate, Vanhell’s Call 

**Trappings:** Bag of Seeds, Potion of Beauty, Potion of Reality, Weapons (Gardening Fork) +6, (Trowel) +6 

## **The Vampire Lorenz**
Three and a half centuries ago, Lorenz was a powerful Jade Order Druid before a vile Necrarch set her fangs on him. Despite his disturbing transformation, his love of plants and flowers never left him, nor his magical skills, his loyalty to Sigmar or devotion to Rhya. He turned his new necromantic talents to the manipulation of dead plants and vegetable matter, seeing little fundamental difference between a dead plant and a dead animal. 

In time, Lorenz found a place rich in Ghyran, and here he built his tower and grew his garden. He saw no reason not to be surrounded by life, even if he had lost his. He grows plants and develops his skills in herbalism, staying close to nature. 

Lorenz’s appearance is that of a lean old man, always gardening, up to his elbows in soil. In truth, he is a lean old monster, always gardening, up to his elbows in soil. Using magic and herbalism he has created potions to temporarily disguise his hideousness. 

Most Necrarchs are touched by madness. Lorenz’s madness is that he is afflicted with a fairly kind heart, even if it doesn’t beat any more. He’s devious and manipulative, but not actively cruel. His paranoia leads to planning ahead, setting up caches of supplies, places of safety and escape plans. He resents being a Vampire and loathes other Vampires. However, he wisely hides his contmpt behind a veneer of congeniality and eccentricity. Lorenz is not affected by sunlight and only feeds once a month. He prefers to sleep on a bed of his native southern Middenland soil; it’s not essential, but without it he suffers terrible nightmares. 

Lorenz expects the Characters to try to outwit him in some way. He understands and respects that. The trick with the Giant Spider is admirable in his eyes, and he’d sooner the Characters and Esther survive than his other guests.. 

## **Into the Tower**
The Tower has four floors plus a hidden crypt. Within the walls, from top floor to crypt, are two hidden escape routes, accessible from all levels, concealed in different ways. Both escape routes are narrow, with metal rungs in the walls. At the bottom of each is a door accessing the crypt, and a tunnel providing an escape route. The tunnels eventually join together, leading up through a hollow yew tree on the Sylvanian side of Spider Holt. 

The tower’s main entrance is an arched double door to the first floor. There are two shuttered windows in all levels save the fourth, which has six. All levels have at least two tall candelabras, besides the fourth, which has a chandelier. However, none of them use candles; instead, brightly luminescent cacti grow in the holders. There are live plants or fresh flowers on all levels save the crypt. 

**Crypt:** Only accessible via the tower’s two escape routes. A stone-floored room with walls covered in murals of plants and flowers. A large stone basin big enough for a grown Human stands at the centre of the crypt. It is filled with soil and 

there is no lid. Any Character who might be able to recognise different soil types (for example, Scholar with relevant Lore Skill like Geology, Hedge Witch, Herbalist, Grave Robber, Villager, anyone with Lore (Herbs) or Trade (Herbalist)) should be allowed an appropriate Skill or **Perception** Test (GM decides the difficulty as seems appropriate to the Skill). Marginal Success is sufficient to indicate the soil is not local. An Impressive Success suggests the soil has the characteristics of that found in southern Middenland or northern Reikland. Anyone who has handled the soil in the tubs on the first floor can also make a **Perception** Test, but can only recognise the soils are different. Access to the escape routes are stone doors, activated by pressing a blue cornflower in the murals ( **Difficult Perception Test (–10) or Challenging (+0) Lore (Herbs)/ Trade (Herbalist)** Test to spot there are only two images of cornflowers in all the murals, on opposite sides of the crypt). This cornflower motif for doors to the escape routes is used on the upper levels; the same Test can be used to spot them on other floors, but need not be repeated after a successful Test (unless the Players fail to understand the pattern). 

**First Floor:** A gardener’s workshop, with trestle tables, trowels and forks, pots, tubs of soil, pots and jars of seeds and bulbs. Doors to the escape routes are hidden behind wooden shelves that swing out after pressing small carvings of cornflowers. Stairs lead up to the second floor. 

**Second Floor:** This is a pleasant sitting room with several armchairs and a sofa. Carpets depicting flowers with their names in Classical cover the floor. Again, cornflowers locate the entrances to the escape routes, although a successful **Challenging (+0) Perception** Test is needed to find the trigger mechanism to open them. 

**Third Floor:** Lorenz’s library. Walls of shelves with old books, mainly botany books, scrolls, and botanical paintings. A large table with chairs is piled with more books on herbalism. On opposite walls are two paintings, each 7-ft high, 3-ft wide. One depicts Sigmar with a cornflower wreath; the other is probably Rhya (Lorenz or Esther can confirm if asked) with a cornflower in her hair. Pulling back the paintings (requiring a good tug) reveals the escape routes. A stair leads to the fourth floor. 

**Fourth Floor:** A room with six windows, full of plants in pots on the floor and flowers in vases on sideboards, a veritable jungle. There are benches under the windows and comfortable chairs. A simple bed has been set-up for Esther, although this is removed on the day of the party. Two vases of cornflowers indicate access to the escape routes in the wood-panelled walls. As with the Second Floor a successful **Challenging (+0) Perception** Test is needed to find the trigger mechanism to open them. There is no attic, only beams and arches supporting the conical roof 

## **Friends Reunited**
Lorenz leads the Characters up to the second floor where they find Esther reading. She is delighted to see them. Turning to go back downstairs, Lorenz says: 

_‘I shall leave you to it. Being a proper villain, obviously I won’t be allowing you to leave. Not yet, anyway. I’m having a party and frankly I could do with a few extra hands on the day. I can make it worth your while. We’ll speak again, but meanwhile feel free to plot your escape!’_ 

The ensuing conversation depends greatly on what has gone before and how much the Characters want to tell Esther. Let the Players take the lead and go from there. If they don’t take the initiative, you can use Esther. 

Esther has been treated well. The Scarecrows didn’t hurt her and nor did Lorenz or any of his servants. She has been free to wander the tower, the hall and the garden, although the borders of the clearing are protected by the Scarecrows. She only seems to be watched when she’s outside. 

She has spent her time in the gardens, walking or helping the servants (who seem happy, well-treated and devoted to Lorenz) or reading in the library (so many interesting books on botany and herbalism). 

If the Characters tell Esther about the Spider Baron, in particular his vision and belief she is his White Queen, she has to decide if she trusts them enough to reveal the changes she’s going through. If they’ve shown fanatical anti-mutant tendencies, she’ll feign shock and fear, and plan to escape later. 

Like Esther, the Characters are free to explore and talk to the servants and Lorenz. How close they are to the party depends on how quickly the Characters acquired a Giant Spider. Here it’s assumed there is one night and a day before the night of the party. They can sleep in the tower, the servants providing pillows and blankets, if necessary. 

## **The Hall**
The Hall is a large open room, with numerous windows, and large arched doorways on each long side. It is attached to the tower, but separate; there is no connecting door. In one corner at the far end, steps lead down to a locked door (Lorenz has the key), beyond which is a large vaulted chamber. This is Lorenz’s magical workshop and laboratory, where he brews his plant-based potions and constructs his Scarecrow Men. It does not give access to the tower’s crypt. 

On the day of the party, that end of the room is curtained off and used as a cloakroom and a place to keep more food, wine, and party paraphernalia.. 

## **The Day of the Party**
The day of the party is a busy one for the servants, as well as the Characters if they choose to become involved, with fetching, carrying, cooking, setting up tables and arranging flowers. Lorenz is about giving orders and advice. He is enjoying himself and only rarely shows annoyance with his servants or mishaps. Everything is set-up by early evening, with the first quests expected from 7:00 p.m. onwards. 

Characters who are expecting Vampires (especially if they’ve discovered the tower crypt) may be reassured by the deliciously normal buffet that Lorenz has laid on. They may be more concerned by the occasional dish of honeyed-rat-on-stick, moth-wing crisps or crystal bowl of eyeballs. ‘ _All part of my Geheimnisnacht theme,’_ explains Lorenz. ‘ _Speaking of which… time to put my game face on…’_ 

Lorenz reaches into a pocket and brings out a vial of red liquid. He opens it and a foul smell comes forth, from which he even recoils. 

_‘You’ll like this, though perhaps not a lot. Down the hatch!’_ 

Lorenz swallows the liquid and undergoes a painful-looking transformation. In fact, the hideous grimacing and twisting of limbs and fingers is all show: this Potion of Reality simply undoes the Potion of Beauty disguising his hideous Necrarchtic features. 

_‘How do I look? Bad enough to put the wind up even the Carsteins, I bet!’_ 

If the Characters ask, there’s no harm if Lorenz has some potions that genuinely cause illusory transformations: Vampires, Ghouls, Beastmen. These are probably temporary, but might require the anti-potion, which could lead to later problems! 

## **Dance of the Vampires**
Guests appear from 7:00 p.m.onwards, a few who are sun-shy appearing after 9:00, if it is summertime. It is suggested you create some of your own, but a few are described briefly below. Most arrive in expensive black coaches, although a few on foot or horseback. 

Some come with a small entourage of staff, blood-slaves or hangers-on, so there are people to mingle with. Most of them are friendly, well-mannered, and have come to enjoy themselves. Only a few are hostile, unpleasant or snobbish. One or two are physically monstrous. 

Esther and the Characters can find plenty to occupy their time. They could serve as waiters and cloak-room attendants. Someone with suitable Etiquette could formally announce each guest’s arrival. Entertainers might join the musicians providing 

polite music to dance to, or demonstrate other skills to amuse guests. However, they are not staff and Lorenz is happy for them to mingle as curiosities for his guests, some of whom might be interested in their adventurous lives. There are tables to play cards or games such as those described in _**Rough Days & Hard Nights**_ . Outside, there are coach-drivers gathered to drink and play games of their own, and folk taking amorous strolls in the garden. Some **Sample Guests** are briefly described, a possible event associated with each. Lorenz’s only instruction is to not mention the Giant Spider: it’s a surprise! 

Overall, though, this is a party, and people just want to just have fun. Make it into whatever you and your Players want and make sure everyone has something to do, perhaps breaking the evening up into segments with specific events. Just try to avoid a bloodbath. 

## **The Other Guests**
**Sigurd Ugenhauer - The Hog:** A massive hoglike Ghoul with a voracious appetite. Lorenz comments, _‘Probably a mutant before he became a Ghoul, but who can tell?’_ Event: Someone gets into a tug-of-war with the Hog over a bowl of something tasty. Find an amicable solution to avoid a fight. 

**Rosanna Breuhl - The Hag:** A forest Witch with teeth like tombstones, creepily friendly to your face, all spite behind your back. _‘Human, surprisingly. Nasty. Watch that one.’_ Event: While the Characters are watching another event, the Hag lures a servant to the garden to suck them dry. The Characters must spot them and come to the rescue (apply Witch Career to standard Vampire profile, even though she’s Human). 

**Friedrich von Carstein - The Fop:** A von Carstein vampire, but distantly related to Sylvania’s rulers of old. Intelligent, but vain. _‘Can’t use mirrors, so needs flattery.’_ Event: The Fop is depressed and follows one Character around, lamenting existence until they have been reassured three times (Character’s **Charm** versus Fop’s **Cool** 65%, five minutes between Tests). The Fop is grateful. 

**Bertoldt Lamprecht - The Professor:** Bespectacled gent, an expert in something a Character is interested in. _‘Brighter than most, but somewhat dogmatic.’_ Event: a Character gets drawn into an argument between the Professor and another guest on a subject the Character has a relevant Skill in (Professor has the same Skill, but 5% higher than the Character). If the Character wins the argument, they gain the Professor’s respect. 

**Lilli von Cartstein - The Warrior:** A mature woman, wearing a sword. _‘Would have made good a Blood Dragon. Unlucky her, she’s a von Carstein!’_ Event: The Warrior challenges any Warrior Character to a non-lethal duel ( **Melee (Basic)** 75%). First to three strikes wins, but only a single point of Damage is done for each. She is both a gracious winner and loser. 

**Joost - The Sneak:** An unnaturally thin creature dressed in dark-blue robes, face hidden in a hood. _‘Marvellous thief. Watch the silver.’_ Event: The Sneak attempts to break into Lorenz’s workshop under the hall ( **Stealth** 75%, **Pick Lock** 65%). 

**Hanna Shygulla - The Gambler:** A beautiful woman with a deck of cards. _‘Careful. She plays for blood.’_ Event: The Gambler invites one or more Characters to play cards ( **Gamble** 65%, **Sleight of Hand** 55%). She only cheats if the Characters do. 

## **A Dish Fit for a Freak**
This should take place after midnight, but earlier if the party starts to flag or Players run out of things to do. Early on, find out where the Characters are positioned and keep track of them. Esther stays close to them. 

Lorenz rings a bell to draw attention and invites his guests (and the Characters) to follow him, leading a procession out of the hall and up the tower to the fourth floor. Furniture has been cleared and a large table placed centrally, upon which something is covered with a crimson satin sheet. Lorenz stands beside it, smiling, and announces loudly: 

_‘Ladies, Gentlemen, Creatures of the Night! I present to you this night’s…_ Feast of Blood!’ 

Lorenz whips the sheet from the table to reveal the Giant Spider. It is on its back, legs spread wide and pinned down with large fencing staples. It is very still, but anyone looking closely senses it’s still alive. When Lorenz gently taps it with his 

trowel, it reacts suddenly, legs twitching, abdomen waggling. A few guests step back with a breathless gasp before overcoming their surprise. 

_‘Now, who among you_ dares _be the first to taste our fellow monster’s_ succulent _juices?’_ 

Assuming none of the Characters feel the urge, the first to step forward is the Pig (see **Sample Guests** ). Wriggling his fat fingers with ropes of drool dangling from his chin, the Pig comes close, sniffing the spider looking for a place to bite. With his trowel, Lorenz taps the point between abdomen and thorax: 

## _‘I Suggest a Soft Spot. Here: the Pedicel.’_
Lorenz moves aside, allowing the Pig to take his bite and guests to observe. If the Characters have discovered both secret passages, they automatically notice Lorenz moving closer to one of them, but still observing the proceedings. If they only discovered one secret passage, then Lorenz is moving to the opposite side of the room. 

If you want to build tension, have the Pig dither and drool until someone shouts, _‘Oh, just get on with it, Pig!’_ at which point he bends and sinks his vile fangs into the spider. 

How you handle what happens next depends on your Players. If they are content to let you narrate the scene, describe how he sucks… and sucks… someone calls, _‘Save some for us!’_ … and he sucks… then becomes stock still… before suddenly jerking upright… slowly turning to everyone assembled… his mouth opening… and thousands and thousands of Scarlet Spiders boil out… 

For Players less inclined to be observers, when the Pig bites, the Giant Spider’s carapace breaks open with an abrupt _crack!_ and the swarm of spiders erupts all over him. 

In both scenarios, the impossibly large swarm spreads terrifyingly quickly towards the shocked crowd. Before anyone can move very far, the Spiders are on their bodies and in their clothing… and biting. And now, the screaming starts. 

Hopefully, the Characters have kept their distance and won’t be the swarm’s immediate target. The question is, do they want to escape with Esther as fast as possible, or take a few monsters out before they go? Do they want to go after Lorenz? If they haven’t discovered the escape routes and don’t spot Lorenz using one, they have to fight through a crowd of panicked monsters to flee down the stairs. 

If the Characters have put themselves too close to the swarm, they may have to fight before escaping. If they decide to go after Lorenz and they are not already near him, ask one Player to roll some dice, with a 50-50 chance that part of the swarm gets in their way. 

Lorenz is no fool and always wary, positioning himself for escape in case something unusual happens. He heads for an escape route as soon as the swarm erupts. If he is distant from the Characters, he catches their eye, winking at them ( **Challenging (+0) Perception** Test to notice). The Characters may have decided to stick to Lorenz like glue, in which case he grabs one of their arms and says, _‘_ Quick! _Follow me!’_ leading them to the nearest escape route, but always seeking to outpace them. 

This escape scene can play out in many ways. Help the Players take the lead. Ideally, Lorenz should escape, but if the Characters end up fighting him, so be it. The Characters may have made friends with some of the guests and want to help them. If the Characters have planned a good escape, let them escape, though perhaps with an unexpected but manageable challenge (an attack by a pain-maddened but weakening Vampire, a partial collapse in the tunnels, a handful of spiders). They might flee down the stairs and into the garden, evading or fighting Scarecrows. Someone is bound to think about stealing a carriage. 

## **Epilogue – Esther and the Spider Baron**
If the Characters bring Esther to the Emissary, they are asked if they wish to accompany her to the Baron. If they decline, the Emissary notes, _‘We are in your debt.’_ If they meet with the Spider Baron, he expresses his gratitude with two light-butstrong spider-silk ropes. Esther bids them a thankful farewell, but asks them to use their judgement in telling Tobias and the villagers what has happened. 

## **Epilogue – Hagedorn**
The folk of Hagedorn are shocked and fascinated by the Characters’ adventures, whatever they chose to tell them. They are saddened by Esther’s loss, especially Tobias. The Characters should realise ( **Average (+20) Intelligence** Test) the villagers fear the woods too much to mount a crusade against the mutants, so they can feel free to tell them the truth about Esther. However, if a witch-hunter or fanatical priest learns of it all, well, that’s another adventure. 

## **Epilogue – Lorenz**
Shortly after the climactic events at Red Moss Tower, the Vampire Lorenz reveals his survival to the Characters, albeit through a ragged one-armed Scarecrow. 

_(Laughing) ‘Stay your hands, my friends! I’ve no quarrel with you at all. You and your long-legged friends gave me more fun and excitement than I’ve had in a century! Oh, watching those tiresome fools and bores as they ran around like True Death was upon them! (Laughing again) I’ll be giggling about it for decades._ 

_‘I’m going to travel for a while. If you want it, Red Moss Tower is yours. Tend the garden if you can. I may come back for it one day, but I doubt you’ll be around. Or maybe I’ll be back sooner. Who knows! Fare thee well, my cunning friends! Bloodless kisses to you all!’_ 

Lorenz stays to chat if the Characters engage him, but not too long. If they attack the Scarecrow, there’s a final laugh and the construct drops to the ground, just a bundle of old sticks and a pumpkin that rolls away before coming to rest. Grinning.

## Guests of the Feast
Feast of Blood is an unusual adventure, as befits the events that surround Gheimisnacht. As such you may wish to avoid dragging your usual WFRP Characters through the mud, blood, corruption, and compromising decisions that must be taken to get through the adventure. On the following pages you will find four pregenerated NPCs with the sort of suitably flexible morality that will allow them to navigate events more easily. 

Vasya Ghorshkov is a Pitfighter from Ostland 

- Kistiane Brockdorf is a Wizard of the Jade Order 

- Ursula Fangen is an Outlaw posing as a Hunter 

- Benni Bottomdown is a Halfling Pedlar.

## **Character Background**
BACKGROUND An Ostermarker of Kislevite descent, Herr Ghorshkov is not a literate man. A Pit Fighter of some renown, it is a point of pride for Ghorshkov that there are very few commonly used melee weapons in the Empire that he has not drawn blood with. Whilst he is a terror in the Pit, Ghorshkov is not unpleasant company when not working. He is talkative and entertaining, sportsmanlike and a quietly pious man. In fact, he is a man in need of a God, for though he knows a surprisingly large amount about several of the dieties commonly worshipped, none have yet to fulfil him entirely. Perhaps Taal will be different. One of Ghorshkov’s reasons for travelling to Hagedorn is precicely because he has heard good things about its priest, Tobias.

## **Character Background**
BACKGROUND Kristiane is an Imperial Wizard of the Jade Order, though she much prefers to be known by the more relaxed title of ‘Druid’. She is an easy going and optimistic person, but her apparent charm should not be confused with naivete. Her love of the natural world and old-fashioned methods disguises the fact that she is curious and interested in innovations. She would be most interested to learn about the flora and fauna of the Sylvanian woodlands, having heard many strange tales. In particular, word has reached Kristiane of odd swells in the Jade Wind, somewhere in the woods beyond the village of Hagedorn. She would be most interested to learn more of this, and a great many of her experiment would benefit from finding a location truly suffused with the Jade Wind.

## **Character Background**
## Notes
BACKGROUND Ursula has been on the run now for fourteen years. Her family were supporters of the Talabecland takeover of Ostermark in 2499 IC, but she took things too far when she placed an arrow between the eyes of Hermann Hertwig. She thought that time and Talabecland would put an end to her woes, but now the Turmoil has seen the province returned to its former glory, Wolfram Hertwig made the elector once more, and the price on her head increased to 500 gold crowns. Ursula plans to lie low in the wilds of Sylvania before escaping to the Border Princes. The further into the deep woods Ursula can find herself, the better.

## **Character Background**
BACKGROUND Benni is a trader in pots and pans, many of which he fixes himself. He supplements his meagre income by telling comedic shaggy dog stories in Coaching Inn bars in the hope his listeners will provide him with drinks and a place to sleep, but if that doesn’t work, he is not too proud to pick a pocket. Recently Benni has decided to try his luck selling his ironware to the peasants of Sylvania, though he has not had much luck drumming up trade, none of the locals much care for his stories, and their pockets are consistently empty. Benni is not an unfaithful Halfling, but outside of the Moot he’s found it best to play along with whatever is locally popular. In Altdorf, praise Sigmar. In Middeheim, spare a coin for Ulric. And out here in the woods? Perhaps Taal is worth a punt.
